S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation, is characterized by developmentally inappropriate levels of motor activity, impulsivity, and difficulty inhibiting responses, with relatively fewer inattentive symptoms. Onset is typically in childhood, but functional impairment may become more evident or problematic later when environmental demands increase, such as in school, work, or complex social roles. The course is often chronic, though manifestations can change with age, with overt motor restlessness in children evolving into inner restlessness, impatience, and impulsive decision-making in adolescents and adults. It is distinguished from anxiety, mood, and personality disorders by its early onset, pervasive pattern across settings, and core deficits in inhibitory control and self-regulation rather than primarily mood or situationally driven behavioral issues.

patient.personality: Alan is a meticulous, detail‑oriented planner who thrives on organized projects and structured routines, even if he sometimes over‑schedules himself and fixates on his hobbies.
patient.stressor: Over the past two years, Alan has been trying to transition from odd jobs into a stable warehouse role, pushing himself to prove that he can handle full‑time responsibilities despite leaving high school early. He poured his energy into teaching himself inventory software and building elaborate planning systems at home, but when he began a trial period at a local warehouse, the fast pace, long shifts, and constant demands for on‑the‑spot decisions clashed with his need for tight structure and control. As the job expectations ramped up, he found it harder to match his careful planning with what supervisors described as the need to "be on your feet and just go," leading to repeated feedback that he seemed unable to settle into tasks, was disrupting the flow of work, and couldn't adapt to the warehouse's rhythm. After losing the trial position and noticing that his inability to stay settled was spilling over into his model building, home projects, and even family interactions, he became worried that something more than stress was going on and agreed, at his mother's urging, to seek psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like I can’t sit still long enough to do anything the way I plan it.”

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: Any time I have to sit for more than a few minutes, like in those long warehouse safety meetings or even at the dinner table, I feel this buzzing inside me and I end up shifting, bouncing my leg, or getting up to ‘just check something’ because it feels unbearable to just sit there still like everyone else seems to do without thinking about it.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even when I'm working on my model kits, which I really care about, I can’t stay quiet and calm with it—I’m talking to myself, tapping my tools, putting on loud videos in the background, and if someone asks me to do something quiet like just sit and read or watch a movie without noise, I last maybe ten minutes before I’m rustling around or making comments out loud.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: My family keeps telling me I’m always pacing or fiddling with something, because from the moment I wake up I’m either reorganizing my shelves, starting some new project, walking laps in the hallway, or checking the inventory app I made, and even on days off I just can’t seem to relax on the couch without popping up every few minutes to do ‘one more thing.’

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: At the warehouse trial and even at home, I keep jumping in before people finish talking—like my supervisor would start explaining a task and I’d cut him off with, ‘Yeah, yeah, I got it, so I’ll just put these over there,’ only to realize later I missed an important part because I couldn’t keep my mouth shut long enough to hear the whole thing.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: Whenever I have to wait my turn, like standing in line at the temp agency or waiting to talk to a supervisor or even just waiting for my brother to finish his game so I can use the TV, I get really antsy, checking the time over and over, shifting around, sighing, and sometimes I end up jumping in early or asking, ‘Are you done yet?’ even though I know it annoys people.
